newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-CLEVELAND BEATS PHOENIX FOR SEVENTH STRAIGHT AT HOME.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-CLEVELAND BEATS PHOENIX FOR SEVENTH STRAIGHT AT HOME.

text.p: Chris Mills scored 20 points and Bobby Sura added 18 as the Cleveland Cavaliers won their seventh straight home game, 103-94 over the Phoenix Suns on Thursday.
Danny Ferry and Terrell Brandon each had 14 points for Cleveland. Kevin Johnson had 25 points and Danny Manning 22 for Phoenix.

"The turnovers killed us," said Suns coach Danny Ainge. "We talked about that before the game. The Cavs don't have any shot-blockers and they can't defend us in the low post, as was evident in the second half. (But) they can shoot, they can drive, they can pass and they're very unselfish."
In Charlotte, Glen Rice scored 10 of his 37 points in a third-quarter run as the Charlotte Hornets held on for a 107-97 victory over the Dallas Mavericks.
Anthony Mason had 14 points and nine rebounds and Muggsy Bogues added 13 and 10 assists for Charlotte.
Vlade Divac had 15 rebounds and 12 points for the Hornets. who beat the Mavericks for the third consecutive time.

In Detroit, Grant Hill scored 20 points and the Detroit Pistons broke a tie with a 16-6 third-quarter run on their way to a 99-87 victory over the Boston Celtics, who took their 13th loss in 14 road games.
Joe Dumars scored 19 points and Lindsey Hunter had 14 for the Pistons.
David Wesley scored 22 points, 12 of which came in the first quarter. Todd Day added 17 points for Boston, which scored just 16 points in the third period.

In Houston, Isaiah Rider scored a season-high 31 points and sparked a pair of second-half runs as the Portland Trail Blazers won their third straight game with a 112-96 victory over the Midwest Division-leading Houston Rockets.
Kenny Anderson had 23 points and 10 assists and Gary Trent added 19 points for Portland, which improved to 10-4 against Midwest Division opponents.
Arvydas Sabonis had 18 points and 12 rebounds for the Trail Blazers.
In Miami, Alonzo Mourning scored 15 of his 28 points in the first half as the Miami Heat built a 17-point lead and cruised to its sixth straight win, 101-91 over the New Jersey Nets.
Mourning grabbed eight rebounds and Tim Hardaway added 18 points and 12 assists for the Heat (24-7).
"We simply got off to a fabulous start," said Miami coach Pat Riley, whose club scored 18 of the first 20 points. "We came out ready to play."
New Jersey was led by Shawn Bradley's 21 points.

In Orlando, Rony Seikaly scored six of his 31 points in overtime, including a fadeaway jumper with four-tenths of a second remaining, to lift the Orlando Magic to a 96-94 victory over the Toronto Raptors.

Seikaly scored all of Orlando's points in the extra session. He had two baskets to give the Magic a 94-90 lead with 3:21 to play and made the winning shot after a pair of free throws by Damon Stoudamire tied it with 4.6 seconds left.

"I told Brian (Shaw), 'Get me the ball,'" Seikaly said. "And he laughed and he said, 'Well, we'll see.' Then he got the ball at the top of the key and didn't pass it to me. I had to get it from Derek Strong."
In Washington, Patrick Ewing had 22 points and 12 rebounds and Allan Houston added 18 points as the surging New York Knicks defeated the Washington Bullets, 92-80.
John Starks chipped in with 18 points off the bench for New York, which has won 13 of its last 15 games.
Chris Webber led Washington with 19 points and 17 rebounds.
In San Antonio, Avery Johnson scored 22 points and dished out six assists as the San Antonio Spurs hung on for an 83-80 victory over the Utah Jazz.
Sean Elliott chipped in 18 points and Will Perdue had 12 and 12 rebounds for the Spurs.
Karl Malone had 28 points and seven rebounds and Jeff Hornacek 25 points for Utah.

In Seattle, Shawn Kemp scored eight of his 23 points in the fourth quarter and Hersey Hawkins added eight of his 21 in the period as the Seattle SuperSonics defeated the Philadelphia 76ers for the ninth consecutive time with a 96-82 victory.
Kemp also grabbed 12 rebounds and Gary Payton had 21 points and 10 assists for Seattle, which won for the first time in three games.
Derrick Coleman had 22 points and rookie Allen Iverson added 20 points for Philadelphia.

In Sacramento, Shaquille O'Neal had 25 points and 16 rebounds and the Los Angeles Lakers limited the Sacamento Kings to just 14 fourth-quarter points on the way to a 90-83 victory, their fifth in succession.
Eddie Jones scored 20 points and Elden Campbell added 16 and 13 rebounds for the Lakers, who scored 22 of the last 27 points of the game.
Mitch Richmond scored 32 points and Billy Owens contributed 19 for the Kings.
